thread:
jen: heads up — ACME (customer) filed ticket #AC-984. They see intermittent 502/504s hitting our hosted inference streaming endpoint after auth token rotation. Trace id from customer: trace=acme-3f2b. Repro steps attached.
michael: can you paste the curl or SDK repro here? rough frequency? region? :eyes:
jen: quick repro curl from their note:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <rotated-token>' \
  -H 'Connection: keep-alive' \
  'https://api.redwood.com/v1/models/gpt-large/stream'
```
They say ~2-4% of streams fail with 502 or 504 within the first 10s. Mostly eu1. Started after a scheduled auth key rotation at 03:00 UTC.
olga: saw similar symptom a while back — upstream keptalives closing during token swap caused Envoy to see rst/early-close and surface 502. Do we have edge logs for that trace? sam, can you grab logs for acme-3f2b?
sam: grabbing logs now. quick paste — from edge proxy (envoy) around that ts:
```
[envoy] [warning] upstream reset: remote_reset, stream id=842, method=POST, path=/v1/models/gpt-large/stream, response_code=502
[nginx] 2026-11-02T03:02:15Z upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
```
Also customer attached client logs: `ECONNRESET` shortly after sending initial frames.
nina: interesting — our auth-cache refresh job briefly pauses auth-proxy instances during the rotation window (healthcheck bounce) which can cause transient midstream connection closes. We should check if the swap triggered an RB traffic migration.
michael: hypothesis: token rotation triggered auth proxy recycle -> upstream connection half-closed -> envoy surfaces 502 to client. But why 504 sometimes? maybe long poll waiting on a shard that lost upstream mid-request and hit timeout.
jen: customer is pretty noisy about SLAs. Can we reproduce internally? olga, can you try a rotation repro on staging with long-lived streaming client and heartbeats disabled?
olga: on it. Repro plan:
- repro cluster eu-staging
- spawn 200 concurrent streams (60s long) with sticky tokens
- trigger auth service key rotation (staging) and observe edge logs
I will run in ~15m and drop back results.
deploy-bot: scheduled job auth-rotation-staging started at 2026-11-02T03:20:00Z (job id rot-20261102-1)
olga: first run results: reproduced ~1.8% streams failing with `upstream reset` and 502, matching customer pattern. Repro root cause: auth-proxy instances drained then rejoined causing upstream connection closure to midstream clients.
michael: mitigation options:
- short-term: increase edge keepalive timeouts and/or make auth-proxy drain more graceful (longer drain window) so existing streams can finish
- medium: route streaming traffic to a sticky pool not touched by auth rotation (canary rotation plan)
- long-term: add in-proxy connection handoff so we don't kill existing upstream streams on auth-proxy restart
sam: for customer workaround we can recommend: retry on 502/504, add client-side exponential backoff and resume token refresh earlier to avoid rotation during long streams. Also we can offer a dedicated tenant pin (temporary) so their traffic avoids auth-proxy drifts.
jen: can we implement quick config change now? nina?
nina: I can bump the `drain_timeout` and `keepalive_idle` on eu1 edge instances for a rollback window. Will need a small config rollout; risk is higher slot occupancy but acceptable short-term. I can push a rolling config in 10m and monitor.
michael: also add a temporary rule to bypass the auth-proxy healthcheck bounce during rotation (auth-proxy will still rotate but not remove from LB immediately). need infra approval.
jen: please do the config bump and post monitoring link. Also open a customer-facing note with repro and mitigation steps. I'll draft a short escalation message.
olga: posted full repro logs to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/acme-984 (private link) — contains traces, tcp-dumps, and heap of envoy logs.
jen: draft for ACME support reply (short): "We're seeing upstream connection closures during scheduled auth key rotation that can produce transient 502/504 for long-lived streaming sessions. We're rolling a short-term config change to make drains gentler and will follow up with a permanent fix. Recommended client workaround: retry/resume with backoff and avoid token refresh at exact stream start."
acme-bot: customer confirms they can accept retry guidance for now but asked for ETA on a permanent fix.
michael: next steps: (1) nina rolls config bump (rollout id cfg-20261102-a), (2) olga to prototype graceful handoff, (3) eng-sre to monitor 502/504 rate post-change, (4) support to send customer note and keep ticket open. I'll own monitoring.
jen: thanks team. tagging @oncall-eng-sre for visibility. :thumbsup:
